title: Barnabae Itinerarium; or, Barnabee's Journal
author: Richard Braithwaite
reason: Burlesque verse travel narrative by a Westmorland-born author describing journeys through Kendal and the northern counties including the Lake country.

title: The History of the Worthies of England
author: Thomas Fuller
reason: County-by-county survey containing dedicated Cumberland and Westmorland chapters describing the Lake counties' places and worthies.

title: A Description of the County of Westmorland
author: Daniel Fleming
reason: Sir Daniel Fleming's manuscript topographical description of Westmorland, including the Lake District valleys and fells.

title: Britannia: or, A Geographical Description of the Kingdoms of England, Scotland, and Ireland, with the Isles and Territories thereto belonging
author: Richard Blome
reason: Chorography with substantial county sections on Cumberland and Westmorland and their lakes and mountains.

title: A Perambulation of Cumberland
author: Thomas Denton
reason: Manuscript antiquarian survey of Cumberland describing the seats, towns and scenery of the Lake District in 1687-88.

title: A Journal or Historical Account of the Life, Travels, Sufferings, Christian Experiences, and Labour of Love in the Work of the Ministry of George Fox
author: George Fox
reason: Recounts Fox's 1652 mission through Westmorland, with sustained narrative of Firbank Fell, Kendal, Underbarrow and Swarthmoor in the Lake counties.

title: Britannia, Newly Translated into English: With Large Additions and Improvements
author: William Camden; Edmund Gibson (ed.)
reason: Gibson's edition of Camden's chorography carries detailed descriptions of Cumberland and Westmorland including the Lake mountains.

title: A Miscellany of Poems, Consisting of Original Poems, Translations, Pastorals in the Cumberland Dialect, and Familiar Epistles
author: Josiah Relph
reason: Posthumous collection by the Wigton poet including the earliest substantial verse in Cumberland dialect rooted in the local landscape.

title: The Antiquities of England and Wales
author: Francis Grose
reason: Illustrated antiquarian survey with engraved views and descriptions of Cumberland and Westmorland castles, abbeys and monuments including Furness Abbey.

title: The Antiquities of Furness; or, An Account of the Royal Abbey of St. Mary, in the Vale of Nightshade, near Dalton in Furness
author: Thomas West
reason: Pioneering account of Furness Abbey and the Furness district at the southern edge of the Lake District, by the author of the first Lakes guidebook.

title: The History and Antiquities of the Counties of Westmorland and Cumberland
author: Joseph Nicolson; Richard Burn
reason: The standard eighteenth-century history of the two Lake counties, parish by parish.

title: An Evening Walk. An Epistle; in Verse. Addressed to a Young Lady, from the Lakes of the North of England
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's first published poem, a loco-descriptive walk among the lakes and fells of his native region.

title: The History of the County of Cumberland, and Some Places Adjacent, from the Earliest Accounts to the Present Time
author: William Hutchinson
reason: Comprehensive history of Cumberland with detailed treatment of the Lake District parishes, by the author of the 1776 Excursion to the Lakes.

title: A Companion and Useful Guide to the Beauties of Scotland, to the Lakes of Westmorland, Cumberland, and Lancashire; and to the Curiosities in the District of Craven
author: Sarah Murray
reason: A woman traveller's guide containing a substantial, self-contained account of touring the English Lakes.

title: Lyrical Ballads, with Other Poems. In Two Volumes
author: William Wordsworth; Samuel Taylor Coleridge
reason: The second volume of the 1800 edition gathers poems set in the Lake District, including Michael, The Brothers and Hart-Leap Well.

title: A Tour through the Northern Counties of England, and the Borders of Scotland
author: Richard Warner
reason: Clergyman's tour containing an extended Lake District itinerary through Cumberland and Westmorland.

title: The Beauties of England and Wales; or, Delineations, Topographical, Historical, and Descriptive, of Each County. Vol. III: Cumberland, the Isle of Man, and Derbyshire
author: John Britton; Edward Wedlake Brayley
reason: The Cumberland section offers a sustained topographical and historical description of the Lake District.

title: Ballads in the Cumberland Dialect, Chiefly by R. Anderson
author: Robert Anderson
reason: Dialect ballads by the Carlisle-born Cumberland Bard evoking the life and landscape of the Lake county.

title: The Minstrel of the North; or, Cumbrian Legends; Being a Poetical Miscellany of Legendary, Gothic, and Romantic Tales
author: John Stagg
reason: Verse legends drawn from Cumbrian scenery and folklore by the blind bard of Cumberland.

title: A Topographical and Statistical Description of the County of Cumberland
author: George Alexander Cooke
reason: Pocket county topography describing Cumberland's lakes, mountains, towns and antiquities.

title: A Topographical and Statistical Description of the County of Westmorland
author: George Alexander Cooke
reason: Pocket county topography describing Westmorland's Lake District scenery, towns and antiquities.

title: The Bridal of Triermain; or, The Vale of St. John
author: Walter Scott
reason: Romantic narrative poem set in the Vale of St John beneath Skiddaw in the Lake District.

title: Poetical Effusions
author: Isabella Lickbarrow
reason: Collection by a Kendal poet including poems on Lake District scenes such as Windermere and the Kent valley.

title: The Excursion, Being a Portion of The Recluse, a Poem
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Long philosophical poem set in the Lake District, centred on a Grasmere-like vale and its inhabitants.

title: Journal of a Tour and Residence in Great Britain, during the Years 1810 and 1811
author: Louis Simond
reason: French-born traveller's account containing a detailed description of his tour through the English Lakes.

title: The Lakes of Lancashire, Westmorland, and Cumberland, Delineated in Forty-Three Engravings from Drawings by Joseph Farington, with Descriptions Historical, Topographical, and Picturesque
author: Thomas Hartwell Horne
reason: Letterpress accompanying Farington's celebrated views, describing each principal Lake District scene after a tour of 1816.

title: Magna Britannia; Being a Concise Topographical Account of the Several Counties of Great Britain. Volume the Fourth, Containing Cumberland
author: Daniel Lysons; Samuel Lysons
reason: The Cumberland volume of the Lysons' national topography gives a parish-by-parish account of the Lake county.

title: Harold the Dauntless: A Poem, in Six Cantos
author: Walter Scott
reason: Verse romance of the Danish settlement laid in Cumberland among the border fells and Inglewood.

title: The Tourist's New Guide: Containing a Description of the Lakes, Mountains, and Scenery in Cumberland, Westmorland, and Lancashire
author: William Green
reason: Ambleside artist's two-volume guide reflecting a lifetime's residence among and study of the Lakes.

title: The Waggoner: A Poem. To which are added, Sonnets
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Poem following a waggoner's journey over Dunmail Raise through the heart of the Lake District.

title: Confessions of an English Opium-Eater: Being an Extract from the Life of a Scholar
author: Thomas De Quincey
reason: Autobiographical work whose later sections describe the author's life at Dove Cottage, Grasmere, among the Lake poets.

title: The Cumbrian Minstrel: Being a Poetical Miscellany of Legendary, Gothic, and Romantic Tales
author: John Stagg
reason: Further Cumbrian legendary verse by Stagg, steeped in Lake county scenery and superstition.

title: History, Directory and Gazetteer of the County Palatine of Lancaster
author: Edward Baines
reason: Includes substantial treatment of Furness and Lancashire North of the Sands, the south-western fringe of the Lake District.

title: Sir Thomas More: or, Colloquies on the Progress and Prospects of Society
author: Robert Southey
reason: Dialogues staged around the author's Keswick home beneath Skiddaw, with recurring description of the Lake District landscape.

title: History, Directory, and Gazetteer, of the Counties of Cumberland and Westmorland, with that Part of the Lake District in Lancashire, Forming the Lordships of Furness and Cartmel
author: William Parson; William White
reason: County directory whose gazetteer describes every Lake District town, valley and lake.

title: The Annals of Kendal: Being a Historical and Descriptive Account of Kendal and its Environs
author: Cornelius Nicholson
reason: History of Kendal, the Westmorland market town known as the Gateway to the Lakes, and its surroundings.

title: Westmorland, Cumberland, Durham, & Northumberland, Illustrated, from Original Drawings by Thomas Allom, George Pickering, &c.
author: Thomas Rose
reason: Illustrated county topography with extensive letterpress on Lake District scenery.

title: Poems
author: Hartley Coleridge
reason: Collection by Coleridge's son, a lifelong dweller in Grasmere and Rydal, containing sonnets on Lake District places and people.

title: Recollections of the Lakes and the Lake Poets
author: Thomas De Quincey
reason: Series of reminiscences of Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey grounded in Grasmere and Keswick life, serialized in Tait's Magazine from 1834.

title: The Lakes of England
author: George Tattersall
reason: Illustrated work describing the principal English lakes and their scenery for the tourist.

title: The History and Antiquities of Carlisle, with an Account of the Gentlemen's Seats and Antiquities in the Vicinity
author: Samuel Jefferson
reason: History of the Cumberland county town and its district, a standard source for the northern Lake county.

title: Visits to Remarkable Places, Old Halls, Battle Fields, and Scenes Illustrative of Striking Passages in English History and Poetry
author: William Howitt
reason: Includes a sustained account of a visit to Wordsworth at Rydal Mount and the Lake country.

title: Black's Picturesque Guide to the English Lakes
author: Adam and Charles Black (pub.)
reason: First edition of Black's celebrated series of Lake District guidebooks.

title: The Recreations of Christopher North
author: John Wilson
reason: Contains essays recording walking expeditions in the Lake District around the author's Windermere home, including Christopher in his Sporting Jacket.

title: The History and Antiquities of Allerdale Ward, above Derwent, in the County of Cumberland
author: Samuel Jefferson
reason: Local history of the Cumberland ward containing Keswick, Borrowdale and the heart of the Lake District.

title: The Poetical Works of Miss Susanna Blamire, 'The Muse of Cumberland'
author: Susanna Blamire; Henry Lonsdale (ed.); Patrick Maxwell (ed.)
reason: First collected edition of the Cumbrian poet's songs and dialect verse rooted in the Eden valley and Lake county.

title: An Illustrated Itinerary of the County of Lancaster
author: Cyrus Redding
reason: Itinerary covering the Furness district and the Lake District fringe of Lancashire north of the sands.

title: Kendal and Windermere Railway: Two Letters Re-printed from the Morning Post
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's celebrated protest against bringing the railway into the heart of the Lake District.

title: History, Gazetteer, and Directory of Cumberland, Comprising a General Survey of the County
author: William Mannix; William Whellan
reason: Mid-Victorian directory with historical and topographical accounts of all the Cumberland Lake parishes.

title: The Homes and Haunts of the Most Eminent British Poets
author: William Howitt
reason: Chapters on Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey describe their Grasmere, Rydal and Keswick homes and the surrounding Lake scenery.

title: The Worthies of Westmorland; or, Notable Persons Born in that County since the Reformation
author: George Atkinson
reason: Biographies of Westmorland worthies prefaced by topographical account of the Lake county.

title: The Life and Correspondence of Robert Southey
author: Charles Cuthbert Southey
reason: Life and letters of the poet laureate centred on his forty years at Greta Hall, Keswick, in the Lake District.

title: The Prelude; or, Growth of a Poet's Mind: An Autobiographical Poem
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Autobiographical poem with celebrated books on the poet's childhood and schooldays at Hawkshead and residence at Grasmere.

title: Memoirs of William Wordsworth, Poet-Laureate, D.C.L.
author: Christopher Wordsworth
reason: Official memoir by the poet's nephew, documenting his life at Grasmere and Rydal Mount in the Lake District.

title: The Northmen in Cumberland and Westmorland
author: Robert Ferguson
reason: Study of Norse settlement, place-names and dialect in the two Lake counties.

title: Cumberland and Westmorland, Ancient and Modern: The People, Dialect, Superstitions and Customs
author: Jeremiah Sullivan
reason: Account of the people, dialect and customs of the Lake counties, ancient and modern.

title: The Official Illustrated Guide to the Lancaster and Carlisle, Eden Valley, and Penrith Railways
author: George S. Measom
reason: Railway guide describing the approach to the Lakes over Shap and the branches to Kendal and Windermere.

title: A Glossary of Words and Phrases of Cumberland
author: William Dickinson
reason: Glossary recording the dialect spoken across the Cumberland Lake District, by the author of Cumbriana.

title: The History and Topography of the Counties of Cumberland and Westmorland, Comprising Their Ancient and Modern History
author: William Whellan
reason: Comprehensive county history and gazetteer describing every Lake District parish, valley and town.

title: Tales and Legends of the English Lakes
author: Wilson Armistead
reason: Collection of legends and traditional tales attached to Lake District places.

title: The Lake Country
author: Elizabeth Lynn Linton
reason: Woman novelist's descriptive tour of the Lakes, illustrated with one hundred engravings by W. J. Linton.

title: The Worthies of Cumberland
author: Henry Lonsdale
reason: Six-volume series of lives of eminent Cumbrians, a key source for the intellectual history of the Lake county.

title: Diary, Reminiscences, and Correspondence of Henry Crabb Robinson
author: Henry Crabb Robinson; Thomas Sadler (ed.)
reason: Diaries record repeated visits to the Lakes and friendships with Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey in their Lake District homes.

title: The Folk-Speech of Cumberland and Some Districts Adjacent; Being Stories and Rhymes in the Dialect of that Border County
author: Alexander Craig Gibson
reason: Dialect stories and rhymes of Cumberland by the Coniston-based physician and author of The Old Man.

title: Wrestling (Cumberland and Westmorland Style)
author: Walter Armstrong
reason: Treatise on the traditional Cumberland and Westmorland style of wrestling practised throughout the Lake District.

title: Fors Clavigera: Letters to the Workmen and Labourers of Great Britain
author: John Ruskin
reason: Ruskin's public letters, written from Brantwood on Coniston Water, return continually to the condition and character of the Lake District.

title: The Geology of the Neighbourhood of Kirkby Lonsdale and Kendal (Explanation of Quarter-Sheet 98 S.E.)
author: William Talbot Aveline; Thomas McKenny Hughes
reason: Geological Survey memoir covering the south-eastern Lake District around Kendal, Sedbergh and Bowness.

title: Jenkinson's Practical Guide to the English Lake District
author: Henry Irwin Jenkinson
reason: Detailed Victorian guide to the Lakes by a Keswick-based writer, covering walks, drives and ascents.

title: Annales Caermoelenses: or Annals of Cartmel
author: James Stockdale
reason: History of the parish of Cartmel and its priory on the southern edge of the Lake District.

title: Memoir and Letters of Sara Coleridge
author: Sara Coleridge; Edith Coleridge (ed.)
reason: Memoir of Coleridge's daughter with recollections of her Keswick childhood at Greta Hall among the Lakes.

title: The Geology of the Northern Part of the English Lake District (Explanation of Quarter-Sheet 101 S.E.)
author: John Clifton Ward
reason: Geological Survey memoir devoted to the geology of the northern Lake District around Keswick.

title: Harriet Martineau's Autobiography
author: Harriet Martineau
reason: Autobiography containing sustained account of the author's thirty years at Ambleside in the Lake District.

title: The English Lake District as Interpreted in the Poems of Wordsworth

reason: Anthology arranging Wordsworth's poems by the Lake District places they describe.

title: The English Lake District
author: Mountford John Byrde Baddeley; Charles Slegg Ward
reason: First volume of the Thorough Guide series, the standard late-Victorian guide to the Lakes.

title: Sonnets at the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Sonnets on Lake District scenes by the future Canon Rawnsley of Crosthwaite.

title: History, Topography and Directory of Cumberland
author: T. Bulmer and Co. (pub.)
reason: Late-Victorian county directory with historical and topographical notices for all Cumberland Lake parishes.

title: A Flora of the English Lake District
author: John Gilbert Baker
reason: Systematic flora of the Lake District by a Kew botanist, the standard Victorian botanical account.

title: The Shadow of a Crime: A Cumbrian Romance
author: Hall Caine
reason: Hall Caine's first novel, a historical romance set in Borrowdale and around Keswick in the seventeenth century.

title: Praeterita: Outlines of Scenes and Thoughts Perhaps Worthy of Memory in My Past Life
author: John Ruskin
reason: Ruskin's autobiography, including his childhood discovery of Keswick and later life at Brantwood, Coniston.

title: The Birds of Cumberland, Critically Studied, Including Some Notes on the Birds of Westmorland
author: Hugh Alexander Macpherson
reason: Ornithological account of the Lake counties by the Carlisle naturalist.

title: A Son of Hagar: A Romance of Our Time
author: Hall Caine
reason: Novel set in the Cumberland Lake country, drawing on its fell farming life and scenery.

title: Great Britain: Handbook for Travellers
author: Karl Baedeker
reason: First edition of Baedeker's Great Britain contains a substantial self-contained section on the English Lakes.

title: Through the Wordsworth Country: A Companion to the Lake District
author: William Knight
reason: Literary companion to the Lakes organised around Wordsworth's life and places, with photographs by Harry Goodwin.

title: Robert Elsmere
author: Mrs. Humphry Ward
reason: Best-selling novel largely set in the fictional Long Whindale, closely modelled on Long Sleddale in the Lake District.

title: Westmorland Church Notes: Being the Heraldry, Epitaphs, and Other Inscriptions in the Thirty-Two Ancient Parish Churches and Churchyards of that County
author: Edward Bellasis
reason: Heraldic and monumental record of all Westmorland's ancient churches, including those of the Lake District.

title: The Recluse
author: William Wordsworth
reason: First publication of Wordsworth's long-unprinted Home at Grasmere, his poem celebrating settlement in the Lake District vale.

title: A Coach-Drive at the Lakes: Windermere to Keswick
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Illustrated account of the classic coach journey from Windermere to Keswick by the Crosthwaite vicar.

title: A History of Cumberland
author: Richard Saul Ferguson
reason: Popular county history of Cumberland by the leading Victorian antiquary of the Lake counties.

title: A Vertebrate Fauna of Lakeland, Including Cumberland and Westmorland with Lancashire North of the Sands
author: Hugh Alexander Macpherson; William Duckworth
reason: Comprehensive vertebrate zoology of the Lake District region.

title: Papers and Pedigrees, Mainly Relating to Cumberland and Westmorland
author: William Jackson
reason: Antiquarian and genealogical papers on the families of the Lake counties.

title: The Old Manorial Halls of Westmorland and Cumberland
author: Michael Waistell Taylor
reason: Architectural and antiquarian study of the manor houses of the Lake counties.

title: Literary Associations of the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Two volumes of essays on the Lake District's associations with Wordsworth, Coleridge, Southey, Ruskin and others.

title: Climbing in the British Isles. Vol. I: England
author: Walter Parry Haskett Smith
reason: Foundational climbing guide dominated by the Lake District crags, including the author's pioneering ascent of Napes Needle.

title: A History of Westmorland
author: Richard Saul Ferguson
reason: Popular county history of Westmorland, companion to the author's History of Cumberland.

title: Thorstein of the Mere: A Saga of the Northmen in Lakeland
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: Historical novel imagining the Norse settlement of the Coniston fells, by Ruskin's secretary at Brantwood.

title: Letters of Samuel Taylor Coleridge
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge; Ernest Hartley Coleridge (ed.)
reason: Collected letters include the Keswick-period correspondence rich in description of the Lake District.

title: The Bondwoman: A Story of the Northmen in Lakeland
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: Second Lakeland saga novel by Collingwood, set among the Norse settlers of the Lake District.

title: Journals of Dorothy Wordsworth
author: Dorothy Wordsworth; William Knight (ed.)
reason: First publication of the Grasmere journals, the most intimate day-by-day record of life in the Lake District at the height of its literary fame.

title: The Book of Coniston
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: Local history and description of Coniston and its fells, lake and people.

title: Rock-Climbing in the English Lake District
author: Owen Glynne Jones
reason: First systematic guide to Lake District rock-climbing, with the Abraham brothers' photographs.

title: Life and Nature at the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Essays on the natural history, seasons and country life of the Lake District.

title: The English Lake District Fisheries
author: John Watson
reason: Angling natural history of the Lakes, treating their fish, fishing and fishery lore.

title: Bygone Cumberland and Westmorland
author: William Andrews
reason: Illustrated antiquarian miscellany on the history and byways of the Lake counties.

title: Kirkbie-Kendall: Fragments Collected Relating to its Ancient Streets and Yards, and the Growth of the Town
author: John F. Curwen
reason: Antiquarian study of Kendal's historic fabric by the leading Westmorland castle scholar.
